Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:20: He said above this, "seeks You early, to cleave to You with abundant love," understood by what Rashbi explains (Zohar, Beshalach 46a), that those who stand with the Shechinah at night until the light of morning - at the light of morning the Holy One, blessed be He, spreads over the Shechinah, and over those who joined with her, a thread of kindness, so that in the morning they cleave to the King with Ahavah Rabbah, which is Chesed, and then the yearning grows even greater for the lover - for until now he cleaved with a small light, which is the nefesh, a lesser love, and in the morning he cleaves with Ahavah Rabbah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:21: He says "until morning breaks" - this is the darkness before dawn, as explained there in the portion of Beshalach. And one must occupy himself with Torah until the light of day, in order to bind the attribute of night to day, and this is the nature of the word "until." And the word "breaks" is to be precise about the word "seeks You early" [ashacharcha], which relates to "shachar" [dawn] and not "boker" [morning] - for the beginning of morning is the dawn, and then the light of Chesed begins to be aroused, and then gifts are received from the King. His words there: "when night departs and morning comes and it darkens and grows dim, then the King is with the Matronita in the secret of joy, and gives her gifts, and to all the members of His palace; happy is the portion of whoever is among the count" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:22: Here is explained from this passage, and from within it, the secret of love as we have explained. And although he particularly connects it with night, and it would seem more fitting that this love should always be present before a person, with the Holy One, blessed be He, as his soul and spirit constantly, out of the strength of love - rather, the matter is that the reality of the lover's yearning has already preceded him by day of love, except that at night this love overpowers him more, and he says in his heart, "when will night come, that I may arise to do my Maker's will and fulfill what I owe from love of Him, blessed be He?" And with this the wording of Rashbi, peace be upon him, is precise, that he takes hold of the word "in the night" - "a person must" - and does not take hold of the whole wording of the verse, "my soul desires You in the night," for the matter of "desires You" applies even by day, but at night one must, out of love of the Holy One, blessed be He [rise] - and the love has already preceded him by day; and he splits the verse with a sharp knife - there are three clauses: the first, "my soul"; the second, "desires You"; the third, "in the night" - and so the cantillation marks prove: on the word "my soul," a reversed shofar [inverted mercha]; "desires You," two rods [tarei chatrei]; "in the night," a minor zakef.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:23: Further, it may be that the reason love is ascribed to rising at midnight to engage in Torah is because there is no greater lover of the Holy One, blessed be He, than this - for he nullifies his body's desire, the lover of sleep and pleasure, for love of his Maker, which is the love of his soul, as we explained, and although he suffers, he bears the suffering for love of his Maker - similar to what Scripture says (Song of Songs 1:13) "a bundle of myrrh is my beloved to me, lodging between my breasts" - and our Sages, of blessed memory, explain (Shabbat 88b): even though he embitters and makes bitter to me, "he shall lodge between my breasts" - and he thereby fulfills the commandment "and you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart" (Deuteronomy 6:5) - with your two inclinations, with the good inclination and with the evil inclination (Berachot, chapter 9, mishnah 5).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:24: Concerning the evil inclination, it is explained in the Zohar, portion of Terumah (163a), that the subduing of the inclination is complete love, since the inclination is subdued beneath the good inclination for the sake of love of the Creator; and for this reason it says in the Zohar, portion of Vayikra (13a), that one who rises at midnight is called a servant of the Lord, explaining the psalm (Psalms 134:1) "behold, bless the Lord, all servants of the Lord," concerning those who rise at midnight - and it is fitting that he be called a servant of the Lord, since one who subdues his inclination with his body's desires and suffers for love of his Maker is called a servant of the Lord, since he serves the Lord and not his own body; but one who does not rise, wishing to sleep to give his body rest, is a servant of his inclination and his body, not a servant of his soul and his Maker.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:25: This is a general rule for all service dependent on love: at the time a person subdues his inclination and suffers for the service of the Lord, he is called one who loves the Name, and is not called one who loves his own inclination; and if he does not subdue his inclination, he is called a servant of his inclination. We find, then, that love is the key to the fulfillment of the whole Torah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:26: Further, a person acquires the attribute of love by rising at midnight, thinking of the great kindness the Creator has done him, that He has returned his soul to his body and revived him from sleep, which is one-sixtieth of death; and were a person to imagine that he had been dead for one day, as happened to Rabbi Yosi of Peki'in, mentioned in the Zohar, portion of Balak (204b), how much love would be obligatory toward the Creator who has done such good for him! And by this analogy - that at night a person sleeps, and sleep is one-sixtieth of death, and how many sleep on their beds and do not rise - upon awakening from his sleep, he must set his soul ablaze with love of the Creator, who has returned his soul to him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:27: Concerning this they instituted the blessing "My God, the soul You have given me is pure" - and "my God" refers to the One who watches over me and to whom I am cleaved; and along the secret way, this is the Shechinah, with whom the soul was deposited, as it says "into Your hand I entrust my spirit." Since, while he was asleep, he was separated from the cleaving of love, sleep, which is death, having ruled over the body - upon the return of the soul, he is alive, cleaved to Him, blessed be He; therefore, "as long as the soul is within me, I give thanks before You, O Lord my God." It would be fitting that with every breath we should be cleaved to Him, blessed be He, and this is "as long as the soul is within me," since He stands above our heads, and this is "I give thanks before You" - this is the Shechinah above my head, as our Sages, of blessed memory, explain (see Kiddushin 31a; Kohelet Rabbah 9:8), bestowing life upon us.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:28: When a person awakes from his sleep, he should be aroused in love of the Creator, who has revived him, and think that thus He is destined to revive him in the resurrection of the dead, as our Sages, of blessed memory, say in Midrash Eichah (3:8), on "they are new every morning; great is Your faithfulness" (Eichah 3:23) - Rabbi Alexandri said: because You renew us every single morning, we know that Your faithfulness is great toward the resurrection of the dead - so far. And my teacher, peace be upon him, explains that this is why the men of the Great Assembly instituted saying "and You are destined to take it from me and restore it within me in the time to come" - the meaning of "in the time to come" being at the resurrection of the dead.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:29: Further, our holy Torah has explained to us the way of acquiring love, how it should be, saying (Deuteronomy 6:5) "and you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your might" - these are three things, and when all three are bound together as one in a person, love will be firmly rooted in him, bound with the Lord.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:30: The explanation of these three things is explained in the words of Rashbi (Zohar, portion of Terumah 162b): Rabbi Yitzchak was often found before Rabbi Elazar; he said to him, certainly the love a person feels for the Holy One, blessed be He, is aroused only from the heart, since the heart is the arousal to arouse love toward Him, and the Merciful One wants the heart - if so, why is it written "with all your heart" and afterward "with all your soul," implying two kinds - one the heart and one the soul; if the heart is the essence, what does the soul do here?
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:31: He said to him, certainly the heart and soul are two and become unified as one, for heart, soul, and money are all unified one with another, and the heart is the foundation of all - and it has already been said, "with all your heart" in two hearts, meaning two inclinations, one the good inclination and one the evil inclination, and these two, each and every one is called "heart" - this one called "a pure heart" and this one called "an evil heart" - therefore it is "levavcha" [your heart, in the doubled form], meaning the two, the good inclination and the evil inclination. "And with all your soul" - it should say "and your soul" - what is "and with all your soul"? Why "with all"? Rather, to include nefesh, ruach, and neshamah - this is "and with all your soul," everything the nefesh grasps. "And with all your might" - likewise several kinds of money. And therefore all of these differ one from another and are called "with all" - to love the Holy One, blessed be He, in order to give over all of this, to love Him with each and every one.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:32: And if you say, how can one love Him with the evil inclination, since the evil inclination is an accuser who does not want a person to approach the service of the Holy One, blessed be He - how can he love Him with it? This is service of the Holy One, blessed be He, even greater when this evil inclination is subdued because of the love with which he loves the Holy One, blessed be He, for when this evil inclination is subdued and this person breaks it, this is love of the Holy One, blessed be He, because he knows how to bring that evil inclination near to the service of the Holy One, blessed be He - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:33: Rashbi explains (Zohar, portion of Va'etchanan 267a) "and with all your might" well - "and with all your might" - the reason is, whether money falls to him by inheritance or from another source, since it is his spirit [i.e., that gives it value to him] - and therefore it is written "and with all your might" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:34: What emerges for us from the sum of the passage, for the discourse on love, is that there are two things pertaining to the essence of love, namely "with all your heart" and "with all your soul," and the third, "with all your might," is a consequence resulting from love.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:35: "With all your heart" - meaning, with your two inclinations, as our Sages, of blessed memory, explain in the Mishnah (Berachot, chapter 9, mishnah 5), and the intent is that he should subdue the evil inclination for love of his Maker, and thereby attain love - as the pious author of Chovot HaLevavot writes (Gate of Self-Reckoning, chapter 7, reckoning 24), that one must remove the love of this world from his heart and strengthen the love of the World to Come, as one of the sages said: just as water and fire cannot combine in one vessel, so the love of this world and the love of the World to Come cannot combine in the heart of the believer. And he writes in the Gate of Love (introduction) that it is impossible for a person to attain the level of the love of the Name, which is cleaving, the great level above which there is none, unless the fear of the Lord precedes it, which is abstinence from the desires of this world - and his words are the words of the living God, for likewise in the passage (Sotah 49a) of Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair, which we shall explain, he says, "piety is greater than all of them," and piety is love, as we shall explain, and before piety comes watchfulness, alacrity, etc. We find, then, that to attain love of the Creator is to subdue the inclination in all the particulars to be explained, with the Lord's help, and this is "with all your heart."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:36: One must be precise, however, about what the word "with all" adds, since "your heart" is [already] two, the good inclination and the evil inclination; and it may be understood by what is explained (Zohar, portion of Vaera 27a) - their words: "'with all your heart' - this is right and left, called the good inclination and the evil inclination" - so far. The meaning is that the good inclination and the evil inclination flow down from the right and left, and there the way of union and pairing is explained; but what pertains to our discourse is what is explained above this, on the verse (Deuteronomy 4:39) "and take it to your heart, that the Lord, He is God," which we explained in the Gate of Fear, chapter 4 - that when a person subdues the evil inclination, he also causes the left above to be comprised beneath the right, and this is the essence of love, as we explained in chapter 1; therefore the addition of "with all your heart" is to include the supernal roots from which the good inclination and evil inclination flow, so that the left be always comprised within the right and the right, which is love, prevail.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:37: "And with all your soul" - they explain that this is to include nefesh, ruach, and neshamah. One must understand what love has to do with nefesh, ruach, and neshamah, for until now we have not heard of divisions within the reality of love, and it is obvious that he must love with all three if he has merited them, and if he has not merited all three, he should love with what he has.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:38: What appears to me to explain this matter is based on what we have explained, that the matter of the word "love" is a person's bond and cleaving of his soul to the Emanator and His attributes; the intent is that you love the Lord "with all your soul" - meaning, cleave to Him with all the parts within you - the intent being to cleave the portion of nefesh within him with the portion of the supernal nefesh, from the place from which the nefesh flows to him. Likewise, to cleave the portion of ruach within him with the portion of the supernal ruach, whose depiction remains above, as we wrote in the Gate of Fear, chapter 9, that wherever the soul passes, its depiction remains there, as Rashbi explains (Vayechi 245a) in the passage "set me as a seal," see there. Likewise, to cleave the portion of neshamah within him with the portion of the depiction of the place of the supernal neshamah. These three realities are within Atzilut - nefesh, ruach, neshamah of Atzilut - and there is also nefesh, ruach, neshamah of the [worlds of] Ofan, Chayah, Kisse, as is explained in the Tikkunim (23a), see there. And the reality of complete love is that all three be bound, each person according to his own aspect - if he has merited the lower nefesh, ruach, and neshamah, he cleaves to all three at their source according to his aspect, and if he has merited the nefesh, ruach, and neshamah of Atzilut, he binds them according to his merit; and the essence of the command "with all your soul" is that he should strive to attain everything the nefesh grasps, so that his love be complete in all the worlds.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:39: Know that just as there is a secret of kisses within the reality of love, as we explained in the previous chapter, so in every world - Ofan, Chayah, Kisse - there are kisses as well; and so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains in the Song of Songs (Zohar Chadash 63b) - his words: "at the time the cherubim spread their wings from below, letters fly from below to above and letters from above to below, and enter into one another and are comprised one within another in the kiss of love; once the letters join, all the levels, lower and upper, and all the worlds, all join together as one and kiss one another in the kiss of love, until they are all one, and the Holy One, blessed be He, is one without any separation at all. All the kisses of love are only in order to become one comprehension, to be comprised one within another without separation; and therefore these kisses are found in everything, to become one comprehension within one comprehension - letters within letters, worlds within worlds, levels within levels, a wife with her husband, to become all one" - so far. Here it is explicitly explained that the reality of kisses is found in all the worlds - the reality of kisses being that causes and effects become bound one with another and comprised one within another, from the side of their inner essence and from the side of their outer aspect, which are the vessels. If so, we conclude that it is possible for a person to have love in the Name from the side of the nefesh and cleave to YHVH, which is the love we explained in chapter 2, for in every world YHVH is found, as we explained in the Gate of Fear, chapter 1, and the Cause of all causes shines in all of them, and each person, according to what he has merited, in that portion which he has merited, there he cleaves, and there the Creator is found with him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:40: Nevertheless, we shall not deny that the love of one who has a neshamah is not equal to that of one who has a ruach, nor to that of one who has a nefesh, for according to his ascent through the levels of the ladder, so his soul and body are refined, and love becomes constant, such that he cannot be separated from the Creator due to his great yearning for Him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:41: The reason is that the nefesh, which is in the aspect of Sandalfon in Asiyah, is close to the kelipot, and the kelipot are a screen separating between his soul and his God; therefore his love in the Name, blessed be He, will not be constant except for a small period of time. But when he merits the ruach of Metatron, which is already more separated from the kelipot, love will be more constant in him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:42: When he merits the neshamah, which is from the Throne, where there is no kelipah at all, being the garment of the King on Sabbaths and festivals, then his love will always be cleaved to the Name, and he will despise the body's governance by this world, which is governed by the six weekdays, and will strip away the love of this world, since this world is clothed in the skin of the serpent, and will don the love of the world of souls, where the souls are bound in the bond of life, cleaved to their Maker, and he will cleave to what is destined to be at the end, for who is wise? He who sees what is to be born.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:43: As the pious author of Chovot HaLevavot writes (Gate of Self-Reckoning, chapter 7), in distancing the love of this world: a person in this world is like a stranger who has arrived in a foreign land, and no one has compassion on him, except that the lord of the country has compassion on him for his being a stranger, and shows him the way to set his affairs right there, and tells him that his residence in that land is not permanent, but that he should prepare provisions for himself to go to another, better land - for that man is obligated to prepare provisions and the other requirements of a stranger, as he, of blessed memory, writes, and he writes: "the proof of your being a stranger and alone in this world is that at the time you came forth into being and were formed in your mother's womb, had all the world's inhabitants striven to bring you forward by one moment or delay you by one moment, they could not have; nor is it within human power to bring food to you without the help of God, nor to add to your body or diminish from it; and were you to bring to your heart that the whole world remained for you alone, with no one else dwelling in it, your sustenance reaching you until your end would not increase by so much as a mustard seed; and were it doubled, your sustenance decreed for you would not be reduced by so much as a mustard seed, no more and no less. And likewise, not one of the created beings can benefit you or harm you, nor add to the days of your life nor subtract from them, nor [affect] your character, your nature, and your deeds, good and bad. If so, what relationship is there between you and the created beings, or in what closeness are you close to them or they close to you? And you are in this world like one imprisoned, whom the multitude of its inhabitants cannot benefit and the few cannot harm, and you see in it nothing but yourself, alone and solitary, with no companion but your Master, and no one has compassion on you but your Creator. Therefore, my brother, be devoted in His service, just as you are singled out in your creation, your governance, your sustenance, your life, and your death, and set His Torah and His support before your eyes, and accept the conditions of being a stranger, which I have alerted you to, upon your soul all your days in this world - you shall attain the pleasantness of the World to Come" - so far. I have abbreviated part of his wording that is not needed for our purpose. We find, then, that when a person reflects on his being a stranger in this world, he will strip the love of this world from his heart and think of his cleaving to the world of souls, where he is always cleaved to YHVH.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:44: Included in the root of acquiring love is the love of solitude, for while a person yearns for the company of human beings, it is impossible for him to be cleaved [to God]; and Rabbi Yitzchak of Acre, peace be upon him, writes - his words: "the solitary one who wishes to merit the level of solitude, so that peace may rest upon him in his life, must attach himself to these three things and distance himself from their opposites, and then peace will rest upon him in his life, and how much more so afterward: these are, that he be happy with his portion, that he love solitude, and that he flee from authority and honor, which is the subduing of the heart. And their opposites: that he not be satisfied with what he has, and not be satisfied with wealth - 'one who loves money is never satisfied with money' - and that his soul feels cramped when he sits alone, but delights in the company of human beings and their talk, wishing to speak and hear idle words, and that he pursue honor and authority. May the Merciful One grant us the merit of attaching ourselves to the first three things and to those who possess them, and distance us from the three opposites and from those who possess them" - so far. In the matter of humility we shall elaborate on distancing oneself from honor.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:45: Let us return to the discourse we were engaged in: certainly one does not attain the level of cleaving, being always cleaved in love, except one who has merited the neshamah, so that there is no screen separating between him and his God - and this on condition that the subduing of the inclination precede it, as we shall elaborate, with the Lord's help. Therefore we were warned, "and you shall love with all your soul" - everything the nefesh grasps - so that love be complete in YHVH, and the worlds be comprised and bound one with another until they become a properly arranged throne in which the light of the Emanator shines; and if the worlds are not bound to become one throne, singularly unified in the ultimate unity, because of a blemish, they will not be prepared to receive the light of the Infinite - for such is the way of unity: it either rests entirely as one, or does not rest at all. The reason is that all the worlds are as one, this one a throne for that one and that one for the next, each higher and higher, and they are all a single stature; and when there is a blemish in one limb, it is a blemish in all.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:46: A blemish similar to this is the matter of nefesh, ruach, and neshamah, for the nefesh is a throne and garment for the ruach, and the ruach is a throne and garment for the neshamah - now, when there is a blemish in the nefesh, the ruach and neshamah withdraw from over the nefesh, since "any who has a defect shall not draw near," and the flow withdraws from over the ruach because it has no vessel through which to bestow, and likewise it withdraws from over the neshamah since it does not bestow upon the ruach, and in this manner the flow withdraws even from the very highest. And this is what they say (Yoma 39a), "a person who defiles himself a little is defiled a great deal" - for when the light withdraws because of that blemish, impurity increases because of the withdrawal of holiness, as we have explained. So too concerning holiness: when he arouses a small measure of holiness, since all the levels are bound one to another, he is sanctified greatly - and all this is according to the aspect of the channel of that soul in the Chariot; from its side it withdraws, and no one can repair what is crooked except he himself. My teacher, peace be upon him, brings a pleasant parable along these lines in his book (Pardes Rimonim), in the Gate of Intent.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:47: We find, then, that the way a person cleaves to his Maker is through the bond of nefesh, ruach, and neshamah at their source, and then all the worlds are bound as one through his nefesh, ruach, and neshamah, causing the illumination of the Emanator, King of kings of kings, in all the worlds; and then it is the secret of kisses in all the worlds, that they be bound and comprised one with another, and likewise his nefesh, ruach, and neshamah shine and are comprised above, and draw an abundance of flow from the source of all blessings.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:48: We have proof from the words of our Sages, of blessed memory, that cleaving is through nefesh, ruach, and neshamah - their words in Bereishit Rabbah (80:7): Rabbi Shimon ben Levi said, in three expressions of affection the Holy One, blessed be He, showed His love for Israel: in cleaving [devikah], in yearning [chashikah], in desiring [chafitzah]. In cleaving, from where? As it is said (Deuteronomy 4:4) "but you who cleave to the Lord your God." In yearning, from where? As it is said (Deuteronomy 7:7) "the Lord yearned for you." In desiring, from where? As it is said (Malachi 3:12) "and all the nations shall call you happy, for you shall be a delightsome [chefetz] land." And we learn from the passage concerning that wicked man [Shechem]: in cleaving, (Genesis 34:3) "and his soul cleaved to Dinah, the daughter of Jacob"; in yearning, it is written (ibid. 34:8) "the soul of my son Shechem yearns for your daughter"; in desiring, (ibid. 34:19) "for he desired Jacob's daughter."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:49: Rabbi Abba ben Elisha adds two more: in love [ahavah] and in speech [dibbur]. In love, (Malachi 1:2) "I have loved you, says the Lord." In speech, (Isaiah 40:2) "speak to the heart of Jerusalem." And we learn from the passage concerning that wicked man: in love, (Genesis 34:3) "and he loved the girl"; in speech, (ibid.) "and he spoke to the girl's heart" - words that comfort the heart - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:50: It is fitting to raise one observation: why did Rabbi Shimon ben Levi count only three, when we find five in the passage concerning that wicked man, as Rabbi Abba ben Elisha says? Rather, the matter is that Rabbi Shimon ben Levi wished to count only three, which are the essence, corresponding to nefesh, ruach, and neshamah. And Rabbi Abba ben Elisha, who counted five, does so because we find that the neshamah has five names, as Rashbi, of blessed memory, explains (Zohar, Terumah 158b): "'and you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart' (Deuteronomy 6:5) - this is the body; 'and with all your soul' - this is the neshamah, which has five names: Nefesh, Ruach, Neshamah, Chayah, Yechidah; 'and with all your might' - with all your money. The Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah will not move from you through all of these" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:51: Let us return to the particulars of the passage: three expressions of affection the Holy One, blessed be He, showed to Israel, since the flow of nefesh, ruach, and neshamah are from Him, blessed be He, to us, and through these precious portions we have from Him, blessed be He, He adorns Himself with us - and He bestowed these portions upon us only out of the great affection He has for us, along the lines of (Deuteronomy 10:15) "only in your fathers did the Lord delight, to love them," which Rashbi explains (Zohar, Va'etchanan 262b) means that He made them a supernal Chariot - his words: Rabbi Abba taught, "only in your fathers did the Lord delight [chashak]," etc. - from this Rabbi Shimon said, the Patriarchs are the supernal, holy Chariot; and it is written "the Lord delighted [chashak]," and he says afterward: "only in your fathers" - three, "and the Chariot" - four; from where do we derive four? As it is written "and He chose their seed after them" - what does this imply? To include, among them, David the king, who is the fourth to complete the holy Chariot - so far, as relevant to us.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:52: What he says, "and it is written, the Lord delighted [chashak]," the meaning is as is written in the Tikkunim (20b), that the Name YHVH is vocalized Sheva, Cholam, Kamatz - Kamatz in Chesed, Sheva in Gevurah, Cholam in Tiferet, and the sign of these three vowel-points is CHaSHaK [chashak], and our Sages, of blessed memory, say, and at the time these are Sheva, Kamatz, Cholam, it is hinted, "for he has delighted [chashak] in Me, and I shall deliver him" - "only in your fathers did He delight [chashak]" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:53: The Patriarchs being a Chariot above is from His great love, blessed be He, for us, to bestow upon them holy souls from above, as Rashbi explains (Zohar, Emor 98b): happy are Israel, that the Holy One, blessed be He, drew them near to Himself out of all the nations of the world and chose them, and from a distant place drew them near to Himself - this is what is written (Joshua 24:2) "thus says the Lord, your fathers dwelt beyond the river," and it is written "and I took your father," etc., "from beyond the river." And he raises a difficulty: this matter Israel and Joshua already knew - why does it say "thus says the Lord"? And he answers: rather, certainly this is a hidden matter - great goodness did the Holy One, blessed be He, do for Israel, that He chose the Patriarchs and made them a holy Chariot for His honor, and brought them forth from within a precious, supernal river - so far, as relevant to us. That great kindness the Holy One, blessed be He, did with Israel was to bring forth a root of souls from the very highest, and no deed or arousal of the Patriarchs preceded it, that the Holy One, blessed be He, should emanate their souls from beyond the river. This is the very nature of the word "chashak" [delighted], that the yearning and arousal of love began with Him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:54: These three expressions of affection the Holy One, blessed be He, showed Israel correspond to nefesh, ruach, neshamah, which He bestowed upon us out of great affection. Corresponding to the aspect of nefesh, he says "cleaving," as it is said (Deuteronomy 4:4) "but you who cleave to the Lord your God are alive" - and Rashbi explains that Israel cleaves to the secret of the blue-black fire within the Shechinah, giving it arousal through their good deeds; and even though the blue-black is destruction and consuming judgment, nevertheless we are alive. His words (Zohar, Bereishit 51a): come and see, there is no arousal to kindle this blue-black light to unite with the white light except through Israel, who cleave beneath it; and come and see, although the way of this blue-black light is dark, to destroy everything that cleaves beneath it, Israel cleave to it beneath it and endure in their existence - this is what is written (Deuteronomy 4:4) "but you who cleave to the Lord your God" - and not "our God," but rather "the Lord your God" - in that blue-black which consumes and destroys everything that cleaves beneath it, and you cleave to it and endure, as it is written "alive, all of you, today" - so far. Here it is explained that this whole verse is said concerning the aspect of the Shechinah, in the aspect of the blue-black fire within her, and this corresponds to the aspect of the nefesh.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:55: With the introduction of the passage we quoted from the Zohar, one doubt in the passage is resolved: how does it bring proof from the verse "but you who cleave" for an expression of affection that the Holy One, blessed be He, showed Israel, when in the other verses brought, the Holy One, blessed be He's affection is explicit - (Deuteronomy 10:15) "only in your fathers did the Lord delight" - whereas this verse concerns Israel, that when they cleave to the Lord they are alive, and does not indicate the Holy One, blessed be He's cleaving to them? But with what we wrote at the beginning of the passage, "there is no arousal to kindle this blue-black light... except through Israel," if so, the interpretation of "but you who cleave to the Lord" necessarily teaches that the word "cleave" also refers back to "your God" - that He cleaves to you as well, just as you cleave to Him, since He needs the arousal of your deeds to unite with the white light - and this is "your God" in the possessive form, that He is cleaved to you, as Rashbi explains.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:56: Further, one may say that the proof of the passage for an expression of affection is from a superfluous word in the verse, namely "in the Lord" [ba-Hashem], for it would have been fitting to say "but you who cleave to your God," and from its saying "in the Lord," it indicates the Lord's cleaving to them; and this is because the souls of Israel are from the side of the masculine, as is explained in the portion of Vayechi (245a), concerning a difficulty Rashbi, peace be upon him, raised on the fact that we find the female pursuing the male, which is not to the female's praise. He resolves that since the branches of the masculine are the ones that arouse, the masculine is found to be the one who arouses, since Tiferet bestows its flow into its branches; we find, then, that YHVH, which is Tiferet, cleaves to them as well, so that He be the one who arouses.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:57: In the midrash (Tanchuma, Kedoshim 5), it says this is by a verbal analogy [gezerah shavah] - his words: (Leviticus 19:2) "you shall be holy, for I am holy" - this is what Scripture says, "but you who cleave to the Lord," and it is written (Jeremiah 13:11) "as the loincloth clings to the loins of a man, so have I made cling to Me," etc. - and we find that just as the verse "as the loincloth clings" means that the Holy One, blessed be He, made them cling to Himself, so the verse "but you who cleave" [means the same]; and this passage is likewise brought at length in the Yalkut on Jeremiah, in the explanation of "as the loincloth clings," and we shall quote this whole passage below, in the matter of the merit of cleaving.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:58: Corresponding to the aspect of ruach, he says "yearning," as it is written (Deuteronomy 7:7) "the Lord yearned for you," and we have already explained that this is said concerning the three Patriarchs, and Tiferet, in which the Name YHVH is vocalized Sheva, Cholam, Kamatz, indicating that it is comprised of all three - and this corresponds to ruach, which is from it.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:59: Corresponding to neshamah, he says "desiring," as it is written (Malachi 3:12) "and all the nations shall call you happy," etc., "for you shall be a delightsome [chefetz] land." There is proof in the verse in three ways that this is said corresponding to the neshamah, which is from the side of Imma. The first: the word "ve'ishru" [and they shall call happy], which is explained in the Zohar (Vayechi 246a), (Genesis 49:20) "from Asher his bread shall be rich" - for "Asher" is the World to Come. The second: "for you shall be" [ki tihyu atem] - explained (Zohar, Bo 43b), on the verse "sanctify to Me," that the word "to Me" [li] refers to Binah, see there. The third: "a delightsome land" [eretz chefetz] - meaning a land that draws from the [supernal] Will [ratzon], which cleaves to Keter, Chochmah - and this is the supernal Land, also called the Land of the Living.
